best_plan.name: p3
best_plan.rationale: Plan p3 had the best observed quality, returning a count of 13 with absolute error 1 and quality 0.9286, while still keeping cost low at about $0.0078 and end-to-end latency around 4.53s. It beat the cheaper p1 by a large quality margin and was both more accurate and slightly cheaper than the other higher-recall prompt variants.

cost_model_explanation: The cost model quickly showed that the sem_filter dominated both dollar cost and latency, while exact filter, groupby, and project were essentially free. Using the exact idx filter first reduced the LLM workload to 120 reviews, and prompt-aware estimates suggested that longer semantic prompts increased token cost without guaranteed quality gains. That guided the search toward concise but more precise sem_filter wording, which is why p3 won.

plan_codes.p1:
pipeline = PhysicalPipeline(plan_name, "Reviews.csv", load_data("Reviews.csv"))
pipeline.filter(lambda row: row["idx"] == "taken_3")
pipeline.sem_filter(
    "This review is overall positive toward the movie.",
    model=pz.Model.GOOGLE_GEMINI_2_5_FLASH_LITE,
    depends_on=["reviewText"]
)
pipeline.groupby([], ["count"], ["reviewId"])
pipeline.project(["count(reviewId)"])
pipeline
